## The Intelligence Curse & AI’s Irrelevant Future

A compelling philosophical shift is taking place on Bluesky and in the LessWrong community, moving beyond the popular "Terminator" extinction narrative toward a more nuanced economic prediction: the "Intelligence Curse." Users like Scoiattolo and Grace highlight a scenario where advanced AI leads to human survival through irrelevance rather than death. The core argument is driven by human greed; a cartel of AI owners finds it cheaper to keep the non-productive majority alive and impoverished than to let them perish. This "survival but irrelevance" outcome suggests a future where humans are starved of purpose, maintained solely because their existence is an economic efficiency rather than a necessity for the AI’s operation.

## 4chan Tech: M43 Struggles and Photography as Art

On 4chan’s /p/ board, a heated debate continues regarding the Micro Four Thirds (M43) system’s market position. While some argue that professional photographers have abandoned M43 for Sony and medium format bodies, others defend the system’s portability and video-centric features, particularly through the success of GoPro. A technical sub-thread focuses on the Optical Low-Pass Filter (OLPF), contrasting the sharpness of filter-less sensors (like the Canon 5DS R) with moire-prone M43 sensors. Users discuss workarounds like $400 Kolari clip-in filters to mimic older moire resistance, challenging the notion that consumers rely solely on phone editing.

Simultaneously, another viral thread on /p/ examines whether photography qualifies as art. The discussion was sparked by a claim that Elliot Rodger’s father, blocked on Instagram after his photos were criticized, only took up photography because he lacked traditional artistic skills. Participants debated the technical versus creative merits of the medium, with one tangential but distinct opinion praising European diesel fuel for benefiting the elite.

## Generative Art and Nostalgia: Code, Games, and Multiverses

Levi Beach continues to showcase the intersection of command-line interfaces (CLI), MIDI sequencing, and live coding on Mastodon. His recent posts highlight the technical workflow of blending low-level code control with musical data to create generative visual art, introducing the "orca" platform as a specific tool for this ecosystem.

In a more nostalgic vein, users on Bluesky and Tumblr are curating a digital archive for *Olympic Games Tokyo 2020 - The Official Video Game*. The renewed interest focuses on the title's quirky visual style and gameplay, positioning it as a niche piece of gaming history. Meanwhile, a viral curiosity on Bluesky asks, "which universe is steven universe?" reflecting fan interest in the show’s canonical placement within the Cartoon Network multiverse and its relation to properties like *Ben 10*.

## Japan Tourism and Sega’s Aggressive Identity

4chan’s /trv/ board recently debated the social perception of Western tourists in Japan, contrasting the "classy" archetype with a specific "Roppongi" look defined by blonde hair, tattoos, and platform boots. This visual was used to anchor a broader discussion on internet permanence, with users referencing a lost 2026-era video of an otaku kissing a Hatsune Miku poster to illustrate fears of a "Digital Dark Age."

On /vr/, Sega’s historical marketing strategy was analyzed as "perverted, angry and aggressive." Users characterized this approach as an insecure bully attacking a passive competitor (Nintendo), with the slang phrase "This must be a gang bang then" used to describe Sega’s forceful, multi-platform campaigns.

## Hardware Reviews and Geopolitics

Visual aesthetics remain a topic of contention in a review of the discT@2 graphics card. Users noted a stark contrast between its "very idealised" appearance in specific lighting and its subtle, low-profile design that often blends into the background, leading to debate over its actual visibility and aesthetic appeal.

In international news, Canadian officials are expressing optimism about finalizing a trade agreement with India by the end of the year, signaling significant progress in diplomatic and economic relations between the two nations for 2026.

## Quick Hits

*   **Middle East Intel:** @Evergreen Intel and @chadbourn are sharing curated commentary on recent geopolitical developments in the Middle East, though specific details remain tied to external links.
*   **Sega’s "Gang Bang":** The /vr/ thread’s slang description of Sega’s marketing is becoming a meme for aggressive multi-character campaigns.
*   **Steven Universe Lore:** The "which universe" query has sparked minor lore debates regarding standalone dimensions vs. shared continuity.

clusters.summary: Users on 4chan’s /p/ board are debating why Micro Four Thirds (M43) cameras have struggled to gain traction, with one poster arguing that GoPro is the only company successfully leveraging the system's compact size. The discussion centers on the obsolescence of the Optical Low-Pass Filter (OLPF), contrasting the sharpness of filter-less sensors like those in the Canon 5DS R and Nikon D800E against the moire-prone but sharper sensors found in modern M43 bodies. Participants cite specific workarounds, such as purchasing $400 Kolari clip-in filters, to mimic the moire resistance of older cameras with OLPFs. While some argue that professional photographers have largely abandoned M43 for Sony and medium format bodies, others contend that shooting RAW is now standard across all experience levels, dismissing the idea that consumers rely solely on phone editing. The thread highlights a polarized view between those who prioritize absolute sharpness and those who value the portability and video-centric features of GoPro and M43 systems.
